technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing Go configtx package and protobuf/config-group model as the implementation foundation; do not redesign serialization or config-update protobuf formats.
Rename AddXXX and UpdateXXX APIs to SetXXX as the primary public API. Set operations replace map values and avoid duplicate slice entries, especially for anchor peers.
Retain deprecated forwarding aliases for renamed APIs where practical to reduce unnecessary source breakage, while updating all internal callers, examples, and documentation to use SetXXX.
Rename ConfigTx.Base and ConfigTx.Updated to BaseConfig and UpdatedConfig, with deprecated forwarding methods retained if they do not create ambiguity.
Implement chained accessors using wrapper types around the relevant ConfigGroup or configuration section, with getters and setters returning the wrapper or an error as appropriate.

Create separate orderer and membership subpackages containing the requested type definitions, update imports and references, and avoid moving shared generic policy functions unless required to resolve package dependencies.
Make removal operations idempotent: removing an absent value produces the same resulting configuration and no error.

Implement the sample CLI as a Go command using the configtx API, with subcommands or flags for system-channel genesis, application-channel creation, and config updates for all supported updateable properties.
Use table-driven unit tests for replacement, duplicate prevention, idempotent removal, chained accessors, namespace migrations, and CLI parsing; use integration tests for generated config artifacts.
Update GoDoc and examples in the same change, removing redundant examples and output assertions while preserving examples that demonstrate meaningful configuration workflows.
assumptions: The repository, build environment, protobuf definitions, existing configtx implementation, and current test fixtures are available and buildable before development begins.
The target package is the configtx/config package referred to by the user stories; package naming inconsistencies in the specification do not require a separate library.
The CLI may be added as a new command within the repository and may reuse existing Fabric configuration decoding, encoding, signing, and policy utilities.
The CLI must support the configuration properties already exposed as update operations by the library, but does not require new configuration semantics beyond those in the existing API.
No new consensus implementation, membership service, cryptographic algorithm, protobuf schema, or network deployment automation is required.
Backward compatibility aliases are acceptable for renamed Go APIs and do not need to be maintained if they introduce package cycles or materially undermine the new namespace design.
CLI signing and identity handling can use the repository's existing configuration and signing mechanisms; creation of a new identity-management subsystem is out of scope.
Documentation is written as GoDoc, command help, and repository usage documentation; a separately hosted website or video tutorial is not required.
Effort includes implementation, code review by the developer, local test execution, and defect correction, but excludes elapsed waiting time and external stakeholder review.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing configtx API, ConfigTx structure, protobuf wrappers, package layout, examples, tests, and any configtxgen-related utilities. Build an inventory of Add, Update, Remove, Base, Updated, and type definitions affected by U1-U8.

Define the renamed method surface, compatibility strategy, chained wrapper hierarchy, slice replacement semantics, orderer and membership package boundaries, and CLI command model. Identify import-cycle risks and required migration changes before implementation.

activities.activity_name: Set API implementation and replacement semantics
activities.activity_description: Rename and implement all applicable AddXXX and UpdateXXX methods as SetXXX methods. Update map replacement behavior, implement duplicate-aware replacement for slice-backed values such as anchor peers, update internal callers, and add method-level GoDoc describing overwrite behavior.

activities.activity_name: ConfigTx base and updated accessor rename
activities.activity_description: Rename Base and Updated to clearer BaseConfig and UpdatedConfig methods, update associated documentation and all callers, and add compatible forwarding methods where technically safe.

Implement wrapper types and accessors for the relevant channel, application, organization, orderer, and membership configuration sections. Add chained getters and setters, ensure wrappers reference the correct ConfigGroup state, propagate errors consistently, and update the existing API implementation to use the wrappers where appropriate.

Create the orderer and membership subpackages, move or alias Kafka, EtcdRaft, BatchSize, ConsensusState, CryptoConfig, NodeOUs, SigningIdentityInfo, and OUIdentifier types as specified, update imports and type references, resolve package dependencies, and add package-level GoDoc.

Update all removal functions so absent values do not produce errors, simplify return values where safe, preserve resulting configuration correctness, update callers, and document the no-op behavior in GoDoc.

Add or revise table-driven tests covering Set replacement, map and slice behavior, duplicate prevention, renamed accessors, chained retrieval and mutation, namespace types, idempotent removals, malformed inputs, and backward compatibility behavior.

Improve New documentation, remove the specified trivial examples and output validation, rename example functions with valid GoDoc metadata, split broad examples into focused workflows, update all examples to use the new API, and reformat code blocks to avoid unnecessary horizontal scrolling.

Create the CLI command structure, argument and flag parsing, configuration file and protobuf loading, system-channel genesis generation, application-channel create-transaction generation, config-update generation, identity/signing integration, output writing, and support for all updateable configuration properties exposed by the library.
Write command and subcommand help, usage examples, error messages, configuration input/output guidance, and documentation for genesis, channel creation, and representative config update workflows.

Test CLI parsing and validation, generate representative genesis and channel artifacts, exercise config updates including anchor peers and namespaced types, verify serialized outputs with existing Fabric tooling or libraries, and correct interoperability defects.

activities.activity_name: Final build, quality review, and release preparation
activities.activity_description: Run the complete Go test suite, formatting, static analysis, documentation/example compilation checks, inspect public API compatibility and package documentation, update migration notes or release documentation, and fix final defects.
